newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower on political worries.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Monday on fears that clashes between Israeli troops and Palestinians in Hebron would spread to the rest of the West Bank, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.88 percent, or 2.66 points, to 299.31 on a moderate all-share turnover of 156 million shekels against 175 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.95 percent lower at 305.23.

"The market has gained six percent since the beginning of the month and investors took profits today. This was also the outcome of investor fears that violence would spread from Hebron to the rest of the West Bank," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.
Hebron has been the scene of almost daily unrest for more than two weeks. Israeli soldiers have wounded scores of Palestinians who have hurled stones and fire bombs that injured several soldiers.
"The market is demonstrating weakness as the political tension rises. Even the dramatic Bezeq deal did not change investors' mood," said Eli Nahum head of trading at Zannex Securities.
Government officials said on Monday that Israel had agreed to sell 90.6 million shares, or 12.5 percent, of Bezeq Israel telecom to Merrill Lynch for $250 million.
Bezeq, the second most active share, rose 1.5 percent to 1,026 agorot.

"The market made a very big move and it's only normal that investors are very nervous," Nahum said. "Despite that, the outlook for the market is still very positive. Foreign investors keep coming into the market."
Kolka added that investors were also awaiting the outcome of a new wave of public offerings. "A successful wave of offerings would add to investors' confidence," he said.

Traders added that heavy trading by Maof options speculators is also affecting trading. "The Maof players are very active and the expiry of the July contracts is expected to be very stormy," Kolka said.

The most active share was Bank Leumi, which fell 1.0 percent to 574 agorot on turnover of 10.7 million shekels. Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the third most active share, lost 0.75 percent to 22,425 agorot on volume of 7.2 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
